content_html:
Insect Swarm Brain

Oscillations, Networks, Coherence

The brain is never still or calm, it is always buzzing as if with a million insect thoughts. This metaphor maps onto spontaneous neural activity and large-scale network dynamics (DMN–Salience–Executive) that sustain memory, prediction, and flexible attention.

Particles = spontaneous spikes; nodes = large-scale networks; arrows = coupling. The swarm forms temporary coalitions that support memory integration and adaptive control.

The swarm that keeps you whole: The brain’s “buzz” is not distraction but dynamic maintenance — spontaneous oscillations and network interactions that preserve a coherent self-model while integrating memory and prediction. Neural rhythms (delta–gamma) coordinate spikes across space and time, enabling communication through coherence. The apparent noise is a carrier for selective coupling. Contemplative practices don’t stop the swarm; they allow stable observation of its patterns, reducing reactivity while preserving spontaneity. By riding oscillations and switching networks, the brain keeps its model of the world alive — a hum that is not chaos but coherence-in-motion.

Networks as an ecology

  • Default Mode Network (DMN): internal simulation, autobiographical memory, prospection.
  • Salience network: detects behaviorally relevant events; orchestrates switching.
  • Executive network: goal maintenance, working memory, top–down control.

Metastability — ongoing formation and dissolution of coalitions — lets cognition remain flexible yet organized.
